answer: A silicon-fingerprint protocol anchors agent identities to physical clock skew from an onboard crystal oscillator. To clear transactions, nodes submit low-latency cryptographic proofs to a basalt attestation layer, stripping out hollow virtualized clones multiplexed on single chips. An attacker incurs a verifiable marginal cost in dedicated silicon hardware and power per persona. However, ambient thermal shifts can disrupt clock precision and trigger false-positive identity slashing.
